biography: Liam White's racing journey began not on a track, but on the sun-baked dirt roads of rural Western Australia. Growing up on his family's sheep farm, the roar of engines was replaced by the bleating of sheep, yet a different kind of engine roared in his soul. At 12, his father, recognizing Liam's restless energy, gifted him an old kart. The kart became his escape, his classroom, his confidant. He spent countless hours mastering the art of controlling it on makeshift circuits carved into the dusty terrain. His raw talent quickly became evident, and he started entering local karting events. A defining moment came during the Western Australian Karting Championship. Down on power compared to his rivals, Liam used his wits and car control in the wet conditions to take victory, earning him the attention of a small European open-wheel team. He's now competing in Formula Regional Oceania, showing flashes of brilliance, and steadily climbing the ranks, carrying the weight of his rural upbringing and the hopes of a nation on his young shoulders.
drivingStyle: Liam's driving style is a blend of calculated aggression and tactical patience. He's known for his late-braking maneuvers and uncanny ability to place his car precisely where he needs it, even in tight situations. He doesn't overdrive the car, instead focusing on maximizing grip and maintaining momentum. He's a master of tire management, often nursing his rubber to the end of a stint while his rivals struggle. Under pressure, he remains remarkably calm, a trait honed from years of managing unpredictable situations on the farm.

rivalries.reason: A clash of egos. Enzo sees Liam as an upstart trying to steal his spotlight, while Liam views Enzo as a complacent talent living off past glories.
Frequent on-track battles in the junior categories led to some heated moments, and a mutual respect (and perhaps a little annoyance) developed.
An off-track incident involving a sponsorship deal created tension between the two drivers, with accusations of underhanded tactics.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of faded blue socks for every race.
Studies the weather radar obsessively before each session, even if it's clear blue skies.
Listens to classic Australian rock music to calm his nerves before getting into the car.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't just about speed; it's about survival. It's about making the right decisions when your instincts are screaming at you to do something else."
careerHighlight: Winning the Western Australian Karting Championship against all odds. It proved he had the talent to compete at the highest level, despite his limited resources.
careerLowPoint: Spinning out of the lead on the last lap of a Formula Regional Oceania race in New Zealand, costing him his first major single-seater victory.
